issue: ਸੰਤ ਕੇ ਹਤੇ ਕਉ ਰਖੈ ਨ ਕੋਇ: who is ਹਤੇ (struck down)?
our reading: No one can protect one whom a Sant has cast off (with our Hindi: ठुकराये हुए).
alternatives: One cursed by a Sant cannot be saved; no one can protect one who has wounded a Sant.

issue: ਥਾਨ ਭ੍ਰਸਟੁ ਹੋਇ: ਭ੍ਰਸਟੁ (masc. sg.) seems to agree with the slanderer, ਥਾਨ-ਭ੍ਰਸਟੁ as a compound.
our reading: one falls from one's place (loses one's station)
alternatives: one's place becomes defiled (our Hindi: स्थान भ्रष्ट हो जाता है)

our reading: one's face becomes twisted (our Hindi: टेढ़ा)
alternatives: one's face is turned away (from God); one's face is disgraced

issue: ਸਭੁ ਕੋ ਛਲੈ: who deceives whom?
ਸੰਤ ਕੈ ਦੋਖਿ ਨ ਤ੍ਰਿਸਟੈ ਕੋਇ ॥ ਜੈਸਾ ਭਾਵੈ ਤੈਸਾ ਕੋਈ ਹੋਇ: sense of ਤ੍ਰਿਸਟੈ and subject of ਭਾਵੈ.
our reading: By maligning a Sant, no one is ever satisfied. As it pleases the Lord, so a person becomes.
alternatives: ਤ੍ਰਿਸਟੈ from tiṣṭh-: no one stands firm / survives by maligning a Sant; ਜੈਸਾ ਭਾਵੈ: as one desires (one's inclination), so one becomes.

our reading: With a pure tongue drink the nectar (our Hindi).
alternatives: Drink the nectar, and your tongue becomes pure.

issue: ਜਬ ਦੇਖਉ ਤਬ ਸਭੁ ਕਿਛੁ ਮੂਲੁ.
our reading: Whenever I look, everything I see is the Root, the source of all.
alternatives: Wherever I look, I see him at the root of all things.

issue: ਉਨ ਕੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਸੋਈ ਲਾਗੈ ॥ ਜਿਸ ਨੋ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਕਰਹਿ ਬਡਭਾਗੈ: subject of plural ਕਰਹਿ. Our Hindi takes God (honorific); the plural verb and ਉਨ (the servants) in the line before point to the servants.
our reading: He alone comes to serve them, the fortunate one on whom they (the servants) bestow grace.
alternatives: on whom God bestows grace, by great fortune (our Hindi)

issue: ਓਇ ਸੁਖ ਨਿਧਾਨ ਉਨਹੂ ਬਨਿ ਆਏ: ਓਇ is plural (they). Our Hindi reads वह सुखका खजाना है, और सेवक भी वैसे ही बन गये, which seems not to fit ਓਇ.
our reading: They become treasures of peace; this state befits them alone.
alternatives: He is the treasure of peace, and his servants become the same (our Hindi).

issue: ਸਾਚੀ ਦ੍ਰਿਸਟਿ ਸਾਚਾ ਆਕਾਰੁ ॥ ਸਚੁ ਵਰਤੈ ਸਾਚਾ ਪਾਸਾਰੁ: ਵਰਤੈ read as intransitive (prevails) and ਆਕਾਰੁ / ਪਾਸਾਰੁ as what the devotee sees.
our reading: His vision is true, and to him all form is true; truth prevails, and true is the whole expanse.
alternatives: His form is true; he practises truth and spreads truth (our Hindi: सच बरतता है, सच ही फैलाता है).

issue: ਸਤਿ ਕਰਮੁ: ਕਰਮੁ is both deed and grace (glossary has both).
our reading: True is his grace (ਕਰਤੂਤਿ and ਕਰਣੀ already cover deeds and doing in the same pauri).
alternatives: True are his actions (our Hindi: कर्म).

issue: ਬਿਸ੍ਵਾਸੁ ਸਤਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਗੁਰ ਤੇ ਪਾਈ: Nanak as subject or vocative.
our reading: Nanak, true faith is received from the Guru.
alternatives: Nanak has received true faith from the Guru (our Hindi).

our reading: No one else understands it or gives thought to it.
alternatives: No one else understands him, though they reflect (our Hindi); he himself, not another, takes thought for it.

issue: ਤਾ ਕੀ ਗਤਿ ਮਿਤਿ ਕੋਇ ਨ ਲਾਖੈ: whose state and extent? The following lines speak of the servant.
our reading: No one can perceive that servant's state and stature.
alternatives: No one can perceive God's state and extent.

issue: ਤਿਸ ਕੀ ਮਹਿਮਾ ਕਉਨ ਬਖਾਨਉ ॥ ਤਿਸ ਕਾ ਗੁਨੁ ਕਹਿ ਏਕ ਨ ਜਾਨਉ: whose glory? (also singular ਜਾਨੈ, ਪਛਾਨੈ among plural ਕਰਹਿ, ਰਹਹਿ, ਬਸਹਿ)
our reading: the glory and virtues of such a servant (with our Hindi: उनकी)

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਉ: imperative or means.
our reading: Nanak, sing the virtues of the Lord (with our Hindi).
alternatives: the Sikh is saved by singing the Lord's virtues.

issue: ਬੀਸ ਬਿਸਵੇ ਗੁਰ ਕਾ ਮਨੁ ਮਾਨੈ: ਮਨੁ as object or subject.
our reading: One who accepts the Guru's will wholly, in full measure (with our Hindi).
alternatives: One with whom the Guru's mind is wholly pleased.

issue: ਸਚੁ ਉਪਦੇਸੁ ਸੇਵਕ ਕਉ ਦੇਇ: subject. The lines before and after have one subject, the person in whose mind the treasure of virtues is revealed (the Guru of this ashtapadi); our Hindi inserts प्रभु.
our reading: He (that person) gives true teaching to his servant.
alternatives: The Lord gives true teaching to his servant (our Hindi).

issue: ਜਿਸ ਕਾ ਸਾ ਤਿਨਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਧਾਰੀ ॥ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਜਪਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਮੁਰਾਰੀ: ਜਪਿ imperative or absolutive.
our reading: The One whose own they were has shown grace. In the Saadh Sangat, chant the Name of Murari, the Lord.
alternatives: By chanting the Name of Murari in the Saadh Sangat, stability is found (ਜਪਿ linked to the next line).
